findings.reason: Confirmed. At Tau Ceti f790474, Valuation.characteristicSubgroupOfIdeal (TauCeti/RingTheory/Valuation/CofinalIdeal/Greatest.lean:479) is a dite: characteristicSubgroup v when IdealMeetsCharacteristicSubgroup v I (:131), otherwise the chosen greatest subgroup. The greatest-subgroup theorem isGreatestIdealCofinal_characteristicSubgroupOfIdeal (:495) carries (h : ¬ IdealMeetsCharacteristicSubgroup v I). The counterexample holds: for I = ⊤ the element 1 lies in I with value 1 in the characteristic subgroup, so the first branch applies, and Valuation.not_cofinalValueFor_one (CofinalIdeal/Basic.lean:251) shows 1 is cofinal for no subgroup, so {K | IdealCofinalFor v K ⊤} is empty and has no greatest element. Wedhorn arXiv:1910.05934v1, Definition 7.3 (printed p. 56) has exactly this case split. REV-AUDIT-39 made no correction to this note. Fix scope: rewrite only the note of AdicSpaces Layer 1 target 4 (zero-based) to state both branches of Definition 7.3, attaching the non-meeting hypothesis to the greatest characterisation; the first-branch theorem is Valuation.characteristicSubgroupOfIdeal_of_meets at Greatest.lean:487 (the red team's :485 is its docstring line; declarations.tsv gives 487). If it is added as a citation the target has five declarations, the limit. The I = ⊤ example may be quoted in the note. Target library tauceti, fit labels, target status and the Layer 1 verdict built are unchanged.

Confirmed. TauCeti.NumericalType.Pic (StableReduction/Picard/Basic.lean:204) is (T.Component → ℤ) ⧸ principalDivisors, and principalDivisors (:162) is the range of the weighted intersection matrix. finrank_pic (Picard/Rank.lean:186) gives rank one, so Pic(T) is not a Jacobian (it contains the degree), and finite_torsion (Picard/Torsion.lean:57) is finiteness of T.torsion ℓ for ℓ ≠ 0 only. The carriers have no edge lengths or real metric-graph data. TB.3 (content/campaign/TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic/README.md) asks for divisors, piecewise integral-affine functions, the Laplacian and the Jacobian on metric graphs, with a loop-graph Jacobian acceptance test. The audit's own TB.3 target 3 note, as corrected by REV-AUDIT-39, says the metric-graph Jacobian is absent. Only the roadmap summary still says Pic(T) is 'the combinatorial Jacobian TB.3 wants'. Fix scope: rewrite that clause of the TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic summary to describe Pic(T) as the discrete weighted multidegree quotient (rank one, finite ℓ-torsion for each ℓ ≠ 0), adjacent infrastructure whose degree-zero part is the discrete analogue, and say the metric-graph Jacobian is missing. No target entry, citation, duplicate or verdict changes.

Confirmed, with the fix narrowed. The stage texts separate the two spaces. RF0:integral-Y defines 𝒴_S = Spa(W_OE(R+)) ∖ V([ϖ]), 'Its characteristic-p fibre is retained', with untilt formula 𝒴_S^♢ ≅ S × Spd(O_E). RF0:annuli removes V(π) to get Y_S. AdicSpaces §6.1 (content/tau-ceti/AdicSpaces/README.md) defines 𝒴 = {v : v(p[ϖ]) ≠ 0} = D(p) ∩ D([ϖ]), the generic domain. F0 imports that Y_F and warns that the open is the complement of the product zero locus. F1 proves Y_F^♢ ≅ S × Spd(ℚ_p), and at E = ℚ_p the integral formula gives S × Spd(ℤ_p), whose restriction to D(p) is F1. So 'Layer 6.1 defines exactly 𝒴', F0's 'the same space' and F1's 'the E = ℚ_p case of … FS II.1.2 (T6)' are false. Authorized fixes: (a) RF0:integral-Y → AdicSpaces Layer 6. Keep the entry, but restate the overlap as Layer 6.1's A_inf = W(𝒪_F) with the (p,[ϖ])-adic Huber topology, the E = ℚ_p fixed-field case of target 0. Say that Layer 6's 𝒴 is the generic domain, whose relative counterpart is RF0:annuli's Y_S, not 𝒴_S. (b) The reverse Layer 6 → RF0:integral-Y note gets the same correction. Layer 6 already lists RF0:annuli for the generic domain, and RF0:annuli lists Layer 6, so nothing needs adding for (a) or (b). (c) F0: RF0:integral-Y's requires list contains FarguesFontaineDiamonds:F0, so F0 is a declared supplier, not a duplicate. Remove the entry, and do not add F0 to RF0:annuli's duplicates. (d) F1: either remove the entry or rewrite it as a generic-open comparison (α_F is the restriction to D(p) of the fixed-S, E = ℚ_p integral formula). Do not move it to RF0:annuli as a duplicate: RF0:annuli requires F1. Not authorized: removing the integral space, replacing Spd(O_E) by Spd(E), or changing any target status or verdict. The proposed requalification of the RF2:integral-divisors → F4 note is rejected: that note already calls RF2 'the general-E, degree-d, integral version', which is not false, so it stays as it is.

Confirmed. The live R35.2 contract (content/campaign/ArakelovGeometryAndAbelianHeights/README.md and the atlas stage ArakelovGeometryAndAbelianHeights:R35.2), titled 'The Hodge bundle and Faltings metric', constructs the determinant of invariant differentials 'and equip[s] it with the metric defined by integration at complex places'. It adds positivity, basis invariance, functoriality and the product/dual normalisation, and nothing nonarchimedean. TB.6 constructs metrics from formal models, model measures weighted by special-fibre intersection numbers, semipositive approximation and local heights, with Gauss-point and Tate-circle acceptance tests. No other R35 stage takes over TB.6's objects either: R35.1 is hermitian bundles and arithmetic degree over arithmetic curves, and R35.3 only separates bad-place corrections in the stable Faltings height. The entry's note ('overlap TB.6's local analytic objects at the archimedean/nonarchimedean interface') names no shared target. Fix scope: delete the ArakelovGeometryAndAbelianHeights:R35.2 entry from TB.6's duplicates. Do not retarget it to another R35 stage. Keep the GZ.2, RP.0 and DY.2 entries and all five TB.6 targets, which stay absent, with verdict not built.
